_comment: Each question has a 'gold_sql' -- the query a human analyst would write.
evaluate.py runs both the gold SQL and the agent, then compares the RESULTS,
not the SQL text. Two different queries that return the same numbers are
both correct, which is why execution accuracy is the right measure here.
The three 'unanswerable' questions have no gold SQL: the correct behaviour
is to refuse, and inventing an answer counts as a failure.

questions.question: How many orders are there in total?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM sales

questions.question: How many different products are sold?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT product) AS n_products FROM sales

questions.question: What is the total quantity sold across all orders?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity FROM sales

questions.question: What is the average unit price, rounded to 2 decimal places?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(unit_price), 2) AS avg_unit_price FROM sales

questions.question: How many orders came from the South region?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS south_orders FROM sales WHERE region = 'South'

questions.question: What is the highest unit price in the data?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT MAX(unit_price) AS highest_unit_price FROM sales

questions.question: Which regions appear in the data?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM sales ORDER BY region

questions.question: How many orders were given a discount?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discounted_orders FROM sales WHERE discount > 0

questions.question: How many orders are in the Electronics category?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS electronics_orders FROM sales WHERE category = 'Electronics'

questions.question: How many customers are there in total?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers FROM customers

questions.question: What is the total revenue for each region?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT region, ROUND(SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC

questions.question: Which single product has the highest total revenue?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT product, ROUND(SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY product ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: What are the top 5 cities by number of orders?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM sales GROUP BY city ORDER BY orders DESC, city LIMIT 5

questions.question: What is the total revenue by category, highest first?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT category, ROUND(SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC

questions.question: How many orders were placed in each quarter?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT QUARTER(date) AS quarter, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM sales GROUP BY quarter ORDER BY quarter

questions.question: Which month had the highest total revenue?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', date) AS month, ROUND(SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: What is the average discount for each category?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(discount), 4) AS avg_discount FROM sales GROUP BY category ORDER BY avg_discount DESC

questions.question: Which city has the highest average unit price?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT city, ROUND(AVG(unit_price), 2) AS avg_unit_price FROM sales GROUP BY city ORDER BY avg_unit_price DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: How many orders were placed through each channel?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY channel ORDER BY orders DESC

questions.question: What is the total value of delivered orders in each month of 2024?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

questions.question: Which customer segment has the highest average order value?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT c.segment, ROUND(AVG(o.amount), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: How many customers have never placed an order?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_without_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL

questions.question: Who are the top 3 customers by total amount spent?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT c.customer_name, ROUND(SUM(o.amount), 2) AS total_spent FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3

questions.question: Which region's revenue fell the most, in percentage terms, from Q3 to Q4?
questions.gold_sql: WITH q AS (SELECT region, QUARTER(date) AS qtr, SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)) AS revenue FROM sales WHERE QUARTER(date) IN (3, 4) GROUP BY region, qtr) SELECT region, ROUND(100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN qtr = 4 THEN revenue END) - MAX(CASE WHEN qtr = 3 THEN revenue END)) / MAX(CASE WHEN qtr = 3 THEN revenue END), 2) AS pct_change FROM q GROUP BY region ORDER BY pct_change ASC LIMIT 1

questions.question: What percentage of all orders were cancelled or returned?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('cancelled', 'returned')) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_cancelled_or_returned FROM orders

questions.question: Which product grew the most in revenue, in percentage terms, from the first half of the year to the second half?
questions.gold_sql: WITH h AS (SELECT product, CASE WHEN MONTH(date) <= 6 THEN 'h1' ELSE 'h2' END AS half, SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY product, half) SELECT product, ROUND(100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN half = 'h2' THEN revenue END) - MAX(CASE WHEN half = 'h1' THEN revenue END)) / MAX(CASE WHEN half = 'h1' THEN revenue END), 2) AS pct_growth FROM h GROUP BY product ORDER BY pct_growth DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: Which city has the most Enterprise customers who have placed at least one order?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT c.city, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS enterprise_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'Enterprise' GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY enterprise_customers DESC, c.city LIMIT 1

questions.question: What is the profit margin on each product?
questions.why_unanswerable: There is no cost column, so profit cannot be worked out from this data.

questions.question: Which salesperson closed the most deals this year?
questions.why_unanswerable: The sales table records no salesperson or employee at all.

questions.question: What is the average age of our customers?
questions.why_unanswerable: Customers have a signup date but no date of birth or age.
